Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{YX}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{XV}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{VZ}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{YW}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{XW}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $X$ to $W$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$  

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{XW}=\overset{\to }{XY}+\overset{\to }{YW},
$$

as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/4758b51fd3dc076059d60e944de0ad8375bb304240365959d4c6cae94f95a535.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{XY}=-a,\,\overset{\to }{YW}=d.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/e942d61c1f51c36dc6cd04f88ff5e37f538920a34c1af5bc780c47691567b668.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{XW} & =\overset{\to }{XY}+\overset{\to }{YW} \\  & =-a+d \\  & =d-a.\end{aligned}
$$
